advances: Supplies one absolute closed mean cap for every finite independent product of the original exponential budget-simplex laws with full integral mean of the form \((j\mathbf1,1)\), allowing all heights and independently chosen transverse-tilt signs. The proof extends the negative zero-sum noise estimate to all heights and then composes the accepted original noise, drift, label-coupling, and mixture-cap facts. This is a theorem about this source class, rather than a final resolution of the locked conjecture.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first work with one row and omit its row index. Every support atom has positive mass. Positivity at a point with \(x_1>0\) gives \(j>0\), hence \(j\ge1\). The slack \(A=L-X_\Sigma-hY\) is nonnegative and strictly positive at the origin. Thus its expectation \(B_1-mj\) is a positive integer. In particular, \(B_1\ge m+1\), \(h\le B_1\), and \(B_0\le2B_1\). This also proves \((j\mathbf1,1)\in E_{L,h,m}\).

For every real transverse tilt, the original height masses are log-concave. Here is a direct verification valid at every height. At budget \(B\), the total has weights \(w_s=\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}e^{\beta s}\), \(0\le s\le B\), and partition \(Z_m(B,\beta)=\sum_{s=0}^Bw_s\). Their ratios \(w_{s+1}/w_s=e^\beta(s+m)/(s+1)\) are nonincreasing. For \(B\ge1\), summing \(w_{B+1}w_{s-1}\le w_Bw_s\), \(1\le s\le B\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,\beta)&\le w_B\sum_{s=1}^Bw_s<w_BZ_m(B,\beta),\\
 Z_m(B,\beta)^2-Z_m(B-1,\beta)Z_m(B+1,\beta)
 &=w_BZ_m(B,\beta)-w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,\beta)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The successive differences of \(\log Z_m(B,\beta)\) therefore decrease. Comparing adjacent intervals of length \(h\) proves log-concavity of \(p_y\propto e^{\theta y}Z_m(B_y,\beta)\) on \(\{0,\ldots,K\}\).

The exact mean equation is \(p_0=\sum_{y=2}^K(y-1)p_y\). It implies \(p_0\le2p_1\): otherwise \(r_{\mathrm h}:=p_1/p_0<1/2\), and log-concavity gives \(p_y\le p_0r_{\mathrm h}^y\), contradicting
\(p_0\le p_0\sum_{y\ge2}(y-1)r_{\mathrm h}^y=p_0r_{\mathrm h}^2/(1-r_{\mathrm h})^2<p_0\).
Also \(p_0+p_1=\Pr(Y<2)\ge1/2\) by Markov's inequality and \(\mathbb EY=1\). Hence \(p_1\ge1/6\). This argument uses the entire original height law.

We next prove the negative-tilt zero-sum estimate at all heights. Suppose \(\beta<0\) and \(m\ge2\), and put \(q=e^\beta\in(0,1)\). For \(B\ge0\), let \(S_B\) have weights \(\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}q^s\), \(0\le s\le B\), and mean \(\nu_B\). Thus \(S_{B_y}\) is the original conditional total and \(\nu_{B_y}=\mu_y\). The letter \(q\) here is the letter \(r=e^\beta\) in the budget-total computation in the proof of `58fe9c7d09f27e78`, and \(S_B,\nu_B\) are exactly that proof's variables. We establish the height-independent computations needed from that proof below, rather than applying its three-height source conclusion.

Adding a larger atom shows that \(\nu_B\) is nondecreasing in \(B\). In addition, \(\nu_B/B\) is nonincreasing for \(B\ge1\). To see this, mix a binomial law with \(B\) trials and success probability \(u\) against the density \(mu^{m-1}\) on \([0,1]\). Its mass at \(s\) is
\[
 m\binom Bs\int_0^1u^{s+m-1}(1-u)^{B-s}\,du
 =\frac{\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}}{\binom{B+m}{m}}.
\]
The integral identity follows by repeated integration by parts. Tilting this joint law by \(q^s\) produces exactly \(S_B\); the resulting auxiliary variable \(U_B\) has density proportional to \(u^{m-1}[1-(1-q)u]^B\), and its conditional binomial success probability is \(g(u)=qu/[1-(1-q)u]\). Hence \(\nu_B/B=\mathbb Eg(U_B)\). The density at budget \(B+1\) multiplies that at budget \(B\) by the decreasing positive function \(t(u)=1-(1-q)u\), while \(g\) is increasing. For independent copies \(U_B,U_B'\),
\[
 2\operatorname{Cov}(g(U_B),t(U_B))
 =\mathbb E[(g(U_B)-g(U_B'))(t(U_B)-t(U_B'))]\le0.
\]
Therefore \(\mathbb Eg(U_{B+1})=\mathbb E[g(U_B)t(U_B)]/\mathbb Et(U_B)\le\mathbb Eg(U_B)\), proving the assertion. Since \(B_0\le2B_1\), it follows that \(\mu_0\le2\mu_1\). Every height has budget at most \(B_0\), so \(mj=\mathbb E X_\Sigma\le\mu_0\). Consequently \(\mu_0\ge m\) and \(\mu_1\ge m/2\ge1\).

We also need a raw fourth-moment estimate. If a nonnegative integer variable \(S\) has positive log-concave masses on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), its survival probabilities \(F(a)=\Pr(S\ge a)\) have nonincreasing successive ratios. Indeed, the sum \(F(a)/\Pr(S=a)\) decreases with \(a\), because each product of successive mass ratios decreases and the sum loses terms. Hence \(F(a+1)/F(a)=1-\Pr(S=a)/F(a)\) decreases. With \(F(0)=1\), products of these ratios give \(F(a+b)\le F(a)F(b)\), including zero tails. Write \(\nu=\mathbb ES\) and \(t_*=\lceil2(\nu+1)\rceil\le3(\nu+1)\). Markov's inequality gives \(F(t_*)\le1/2\), so \(F(nt_*)\le2^{-n}\). Thus
\[
 \mathbb E(S+1)^4
 \le t_*^4\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)^4 2^{-n}
 =300t_*^4\le24300(\nu+1)^4.
\]
The series value follows by four differentiations of the geometric series. Each \(S_B\) is log-concave, including the point mass at \(B=0\). Each original conditional total is stochastically at most \(S_{B_0}\), since it is the same positive weighted law truncated to a smaller prefix. For \(1\le r\le4\), power means therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E(X_\Sigma/m)^r
 &\le24300^{r/4}\bigl((\mu_0+1)/m\bigr)^r\\
 &\le24300\bigl((\mu_0+1)/m\bigr)^4
 \le24300\cdot81(\mu_1/m)^4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \((\mu_0+1)/m\ge1\), and \(\mu_0+1\le2\mu_1+1\le3\mu_1\).

Take any \(\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(\sum_r b_r=0\), and put \(Q=\sum_r b_r^2\), \(Q_4=\sum_r b_r^4\), and \(N_\perp=\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf X\). The coefficients \(\mathbf b,Q,Q_4\) are those in the composition computation of `58fe9c7d09f27e78`; its zero-sum noise \(N\) is called \(N_\perp\) here, reserving \(N\) for the full row noise below. Given \((Y,X_\Sigma)=(y,s)\), the transverse vector is uniform on the complete compositions \(\mathbf C_s\) of \(s\) into \(m\) parts. Its directional mean is zero. The uniform-composition identities used in that accepted proof give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf C_s)^2
 &=\frac{s(s+m)}{m(m+1)}Q,\\
 \mathbb E(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf C_s)^4
 &\le Q^2\bigl(9(s/m)^4+18(s/m)^3+10(s/m)^2+s/m\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Their objects have the same normalization here: every complete composition has mass \(1/\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}\). The calculation concerns each fixed nonnegative total \(s\), uses \(Q_4\le Q^2\), and has no restriction on the height support or tilt. Thus its applicability does not use the three-height hypothesis of that predecessor's source theorem.

Averaging these identities under the original law gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EN_\perp^4&\le38\cdot24300\cdot81\,Q^2(\mu_1/m)^4
              =74795400\,Q^2(\mu_1/m)^4,\\
 \mathbb EN_\perp^2&=\frac{Q}{m(m+1)}\mathbb E[X_\Sigma(X_\Sigma+m)]
       \ge\frac{Q\mu_1^2}{6m(m+1)}
       \ge\frac Q{12}(\mu_1/m)^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second line uses the original \(p_1\ge1/6\) and Jensen's inequality, followed by \(m/(m+1)\ge1/2\). It follows that
\(\mathbb EN_\perp^4\le10770537600(\mathbb EN_\perp^2)^2\le12\cdot10^9(\mathbb EN_\perp^2)^2\).
If \(Q=0\), this holds with both sides zero. For \(m=1\), every zero-sum coefficient vector is zero, so the same bound holds directly.

Now let \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^m\) be arbitrary, put \(\bar a=m^{-1}\sum_r a_r\), \(b_r=a_r-\bar a\), and retain \(N_\perp=\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf X\). Define the original row noise \(N=\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y])\), the total noise \(U=X_\Sigma-\mu_Y\), and \(\sigma^2=\mathbb EN^2\). Permutation symmetry gives \(\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y]=(\mu_Y/m)\mathbf1\), so \(N=\bar aU+N_\perp\). Since \(\mathbb E[N_\perp\mid Y,X_\Sigma]=0\), the cross term vanishes and
\(\sigma^2=\bar a^2\mathbb EU^2+\mathbb EN_\perp^2\).

For \(\beta<0\), accepted fact `c247c213420636e1` applies to exactly this original full-mean law at every \(K\ge2\), and gives \(\mathbb EU^4\le2^{121}(\mathbb EU^2)^2\). Combining it with the all-height zero-sum estimate just proved and \(|x+y|^4\le8(|x|^4+|y|^4)\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EN^4
 &\le8\left(2^{121}\bar a^4(\mathbb EU^2)^2
                    +12\cdot10^9(\mathbb EN_\perp^2)^2\right)\\
 &\le2^{124}\left[\bar a^4(\mathbb EU^2)^2+(\mathbb EN_\perp^2)^2\right]
 \le2^{124}\sigma^4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(\beta\ge0\), accepted fact `fc05e99e54e6cdad` concerns the same original noise \(N\) and gives \(\mathbb EN^4\le1200000000000\,\sigma^4\le2^{124}\sigma^4\). Thus the same row constant works at every tilt, including zero.

Put \(s=\mu_1-\mu_0\) and define the row drift and height part by
\[
 V=\bar a[\mu_Y-mj-s(Y-1)],\qquad
 W=(c+\bar a s)(Y-1).
\]
The bracket in \(V\) is exactly the scalar drift called \(V\) in accepted fact `128749b1a260f222`; the present \(V\) is its scaling by \(\bar a\). That accepted fact applies because \(j\ge1\), and gives \(\mathbb EV=0\) and \(\mathbb EV^4\le2^{55}\bar a^4v_1^2\). This also includes \(\beta=0\), when the bracket vanishes identically. The orthogonal variance identity above and the original middle mass give \(\sigma^2\ge\bar a^2p_1v_1\ge\bar a^2v_1/6\). Therefore
\(\mathbb EV^4\le36\cdot2^{55}\sigma^4\le2^{124}\sigma^4\).
No division by \(\bar a\) or \(\sigma\) was used, so this includes their zero cases. Finally the exact directional decomposition is
\(\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-j\mathbf1)+c(Y-1)=W+V+N\).

Restore the row indices. Each original height law \(p_{i,y}\) is log-concave with finite contiguous positive support and mean one, as proved above. Apply accepted fact `3a60a638a17036a8` to these original height marginals and their original transverse kernels \(K_{i,y}\). Let \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}\) be the label called \(\Lambda_i\) in that fact; it is unrelated to the locked problem's mixed-integer lattice. Its mixture weights and component height laws are \(\pi_{i,\ell}\) and \(\nu^{(i,\ell)}\). Attach the labels by independent conditional draws with
\[
 \Pr(\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}=\ell\mid\mathbf X_i,Y_i=y)
 =\frac{\pi_{i,\ell}\nu^{(i,\ell)}_y}{p_{i,y}},
 \qquad
 \Pr(\mathbf X_i\in A,Y_i=y,\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}=\ell)
 =\pi_{i,\ell}\nu^{(i,\ell)}_yK_{i,y}(A).
\]
Every denominator is positive on the original height support. By the accepted coupling theorem, summing over labels recovers exactly the original joint product law and every original transverse kernel is unchanged. The augmented row experiments are independent; conditional on the labels, their heights are independent with the displayed component laws of mean one. For \(K_0:=236844\), that fact gives, with \(W_i=(c_i+\bar a_i s_i)(Y_i-1)\),
\[
 \mathbb E[W_i\mid\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[W_i^4\mid\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}]
 \le K_0\bigl(\mathbb E[W_i^2\mid\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}]\bigr)^2.
\]
It also gives \(\mathbb E[N_i\mid Y_i,\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}]=0\). All conditional and unconditional moments here are finite, since every row and label support is finite.

To apply accepted fact `828c61552093316c`, take its row latent element to be \(\mathcal Y_i:=(Y_i,\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i})\), and its label to be \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{lab},i}\). Its notation \(Y_i\) for a latent random element is thus mapped to the augmented pair \(\mathcal Y_i\), rather than to the bare original height. In particular the label sigma-algebra is contained in \(\sigma(\mathcal Y_i)\). Both \(W_i\) and \(V_i\) are measurable in this latent element, \(N_i\) is conditionally centered given it, and the full experiments \((\mathcal Y_i,N_i)\) are independent across rows. The unconditional row noise and drift bounds remain exactly those just proved under the original laws, since deleting the labels recovers those laws. No common conditional transverse mean is asserted or required.

Use the independent-sum conclusion of `828c61552093316c` once with its row count equal to \(k\), its moment constant \(K\) equal to \(K_{\mathrm{mom}}:=2^{124}\), and its height regularity constant equal to \(K_0=236844\). The support heights \(K_i\) are unrelated to its moment constant. All its hypotheses now hold, and it gives
\[
 \min\left\{\Pr\left(\sum_i(W_i+V_i+N_i)\ge0\right),
             \Pr\left(\sum_i(W_i+V_i+N_i)\le0\right)\right\}
 \ge\frac{1}{9\cdot2^{278}\cdot236844^4}>2^{-354}.
\]
Indeed \(9<2^4\) and \(236844<2^{18}\). If \(\sum_i\sigma_i^2=0\), the same accepted result instead gives the stronger bound \(1/(4K_0)\); this covers the entirely zero-noise case and all zero conditional variances. The exact row decompositions identify the displayed sum with \(T\). Its probability law is the original product marginal of the augmented coupling, proving the two closed sign bounds in the statement.

The full joint mean lies in the product support by the first paragraph. For any closed affine halfspace containing it, the parallel halfspace whose boundary passes through the mean is contained in it. The probability of this latter halfspace is one of the proved closed sign probabilities for a suitable choice of the coefficient vectors and height coefficients. This proves the stated halfspace consequence.
statement:
Let \(k\ge1\) be an integer. For each \(1\le i\le k\), let \(m_i,h_i,L_i\) be positive integers with \(K_i:=\lfloor L_i/h_i\rfloor\ge2\), and let \(\beta_i,\theta_i\in\mathbb R\) be finite. Take the rows \((\mathbf X_i,Y_i)\) independently, with their original strictly positive laws
\[
 p_i(\mathbf x,y)=\frac{\exp(\beta_i\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}x_r+\theta_i y)}{\mathcal Z_i},
 \qquad
 E_{L_i,h_i,m_i}=\left\{(\mathbf x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m_i+1}:
                     \sum_{r=1}^{m_i}x_r+h_i y\le L_i\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal Z_i\) is the sum of the displayed weights over the support. Suppose \(\mathbb E(\mathbf X_i,Y_i)=(j_i\mathbf1,1)\) with \(j_i\in\mathbb Z\). Each row has one common transverse tilt \(\beta_i\); its value and sign may differ between rows.

For every \(\mathbf a_i\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\) and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\), put
\[
 T=\sum_{i=1}^k\left[\mathbf a_i\cdot(\mathbf X_i-j_i\mathbf1)
                                 +c_i(Y_i-1)\right].
\]
Then \(\min\{\Pr(T\ge0),\Pr(T\le0)\}\ge2^{-354}\). Consequently the joint mean belongs to the product support, and every closed affine halfspace containing it has original product probability at least \(2^{-354}\). The assertion includes \(m_i=1\), \(\beta_i=0\), zero coefficients or noise variances, and final budgets \(L_i-h_iK_i=0\).

For each row, \(X_{\Sigma,i}=\sum_rX_{i,r}\), \(B_{i,y}=L_i-h_i y\), \(p_{i,y}=\Pr(Y_i=y)\), \(\mu_{i,y}=\mathbb E[X_{\Sigma,i}\mid Y_i=y]\), and \(v_{i,y}=\operatorname{Var}(X_{\Sigma,i}\mid Y_i=y)\) have the transverse-total, original-budget, height-mass, conditional-total-mean, and conditional-total-variance meanings used in `128749b1a260f222` and `c247c213420636e1`. The letter \(p_i\) for the original joint law is an alias of the letter \(R\) in `128749b1a260f222` and `58fe9c7d09f27e78`. All noise estimates below are averaged under these original joint laws.
